findings.title: Three validation walls (exact-sum, duplicate-advance, not-this-claimant) and the door/birth-trigger/read logic were written with only ONE driving test, then left untested for several commits before their test cells landed with zero accompanying code change
findings.evidence: Commit 84cf37952 (`feat(db): #931 a staff expense claim discharges several advances...`) adds packages/db/migrations/0301_staff_expense_claim_allocations.sql at 1410 of its eventual 1479 lines (95%) in one commit -- including `_assert_claim_basis`'s three NEW branches (the exact-sum check at 0301.sql:618-627, the distinct-advance check at 0301.sql:601-607, and the not-this-claimant ownership check at 0301.sql:787-797), the door's allocation insert, and the birth trigger's per-allocation loop -- against exactly ONE new test (`p931.two`, which exercises none of those three branches: it uses two advances on one account, both belonging to the same claimant, with an exact sum). The corresponding test cells (`p931.sum`, `p931.twice`, `p931.claimant`, plus the replay/canonicalisation cells `p931.single` and `p931.split.conflict`) do not land until commit a29f8be20 (`test(db): #931 the allocation list's own walls...`), which is a TEST-ONLY commit (140 lines, zero production-code lines) arriving after two intervening commits (ee159783f, 89bffb2a1) that touch unrelated parts of the same walls. Between 84cf37952 and a29f8be20 the exact-sum, distinct and not-this-claimant refusal code was live on the branch with no JS test and no migration tail assertion exercising the refusal paths (the migration's own tail T.1-T.6 only probes catalog shape and one VALID single-advance claim -- see 0301.sql:1398-1432 -- never a malformed one), i.e. speculative code for tests not yet written, which WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 states directly: 'No speculative code for tests you have not written' and 'One slice at a time: one test -> see it red for the right reason -> the minimal code that turns it green.' The ticket's own report (wave4-lane02-ticket931.md, 'The vacuity control') is candid that slice D added 'no new code -- the walls were written in slice A as one migration,' and compensates after the fact with a deliberate-break-and-restore vacuity control -- which proves the assertions are load-bearing, but is a different guarantee from red-before-green ordering and does not retroactively satisfy it. By contrast, slices B (ee159783f, the shortfall_cents field) and C (89bffb2a1, the per-account credit-leg grouping) in the SAME migration file DO show genuine one-test-then-minimal-code increments, so the team clearly had the option to slice the validator's walls the same way and did not for this subset.
findings.failure_scenario: This is a process finding, not a live defect: I re-ran the 9 cells in staff-expense-claim-allocations.test.mjs against the lane database and all 9 pass. The risk this rule guards against is exactly what the wave's own house law names elsewhere as the cost of horizontal slicing -- untested branches (here, three refusal paths spanning several hundred SQL lines) sitting in a migration for multiple commits before anything drives them red, during which a defect in any of the three walls (e.g. a field-path typo in the not-this-claimant refusal, or an off-by-one in the distinct-advance duplicate probe) would have gone unnoticed until the batched test commit, rather than being caught at the moment it was introduced.
findings.required_fix: None required post hoc since the walls are now covered and proved load-bearing by the vacuity control; flagged so the integrator can decide whether to ask for tighter slicing on future single-migration-file tickets in this wave, and so the pattern is not read as the house norm from this ticket's report alone.

findings.kind: smell: Duplicated Code (Fowler ch.3, baseline judgement call)
findings.title: The "still outstanding" advance predicate is duplicated verbatim across two components instead of being extracted
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/registers/staff-advances-register.tsx:76: `const outstandingAdvances = data.summary.advances.filter((a) => a.outstanding_cents > 0 && !a.voided);` and apps/web/components/accounting/staff-expense-claim-form.tsx:264-266 (added by #930): `return advancesRead.data.advances.filter((a) => a.account_code === code && a.outstanding_cents > 0 && !a.voided);` -- the `outstanding_cents > 0 && !a.voided` clause is copy-pasted rather than factored into one shared predicate (e.g. an `isOutstandingAdvance(a)` helper in lib/registers/staff-advances-doors.ts) that both call sites would import. The form's own comment (staff-expense-claim-form.tsx:255-258) explicitly calls out that this is meant to be "the EXACT predicate" the register uses, which is exactly the situation Fowler's Duplicated Code smell names: the same logic shape asserted by comment to be identical in two places, with nothing enforcing that identity if one side changes.
findings.failure_scenario: If a future ticket changes what "still outstanding" means (e.g. adds a third condition, or changes voided handling), a person can update staff-advances-register.tsx and, relying on the comment rather than a shared symbol, forget the second site in staff-expense-claim-form.tsx -- the two surfaces would then silently disagree about which advances are selectable, which is precisely the drift both #930's and #931's own commentary say they are trying to avoid.
findings.required_fix: Extract the predicate into a small shared function in lib/registers/staff-advances-doors.ts (or a sibling module) and call it from both components; not required before merge, offered as a judgement call per the smell baseline, not a hard violation.
